methodology: exception-capture-completeness-v0.1.0: rules match deterministic scenario signals. Global block signals suppress outbound packets. Matching rules emit candidate packet classes; they do not prove source truth or authorize repo mutation.

rules.description: A repo created or discovered a reusable digital asset that may help other repos.

emit.rationale: Reusable assets should be suggested to DAD with provenance and pointers so the library can classify them.

applies_when: The asset is reusable beyond the source repo and can be described without raw private content.
does_not_apply_when: The artifact is routine source code, private-only, duplicate, or cannot be summarized safely.
rules.danger_if_missed: DAD misses useful assets and future repos repeat work.

rules.description: A repeated coding, testing, red-team, or governance workflow should become a harness candidate.

emit.rationale: Coding-improvement harnesses should enter DAD's harness library as candidate capabilities.

applies_when: The workflow can be reused by Codex, Claude, Cursor, or future agents.
does_not_apply_when: The workflow is one-off, unvalidated, or requires private raw data.
rules.danger_if_missed: High-leverage coding improvements stay trapped in one repo or chat.

rules.description: A repo found a Python, Rust, mixed-language, or future-language coding technique, tool, library, codebase pattern, or proof operation that may improve AI coding.

emit.rationale: Language-frontier signals should enter DAD as pointer-only candidate evidence routed to language assets, coding harnesses, or tactic radar before any guidance changes.

applies_when: A repo validates, falsifies, or discovers a Python, Rust, mixed-language, or future-language coding improvement that could help other AI coding agents.
A codebase or source-watch pass finds an underused operation or proof surface that generic AI agents are likely to miss.
does_not_apply_when: The evidence is copied third-party docs, copied source, raw benchmark tables, raw logs, private rows, or credentials.
The finding cannot name a source pointer, applicability limit, proof surface, and local validation or eval idea.
rules.danger_if_missed: DAD's language guidance and harness library fall behind real repo learning, and future agents keep coding from generic GitHub-shaped habits instead of local proof surfaces.

rules.description: A repo created, updated, retired, or replaced an agent skill or skill pointer.

emit.rationale: DAD is the skill library and must know lifecycle updates without copying full skills into repos.

applies_when: The skill affects future AI agent behavior or should be checked out by other repos.
does_not_apply_when: The change is private scratch prompt text or not safe to summarize.
rules.danger_if_missed: Agents use stale or conflicting skill guidance.

rules.description: A reusable template, managed block, or downstream pointer contract changed.

emit.rationale: Repos using templates need candidate upgrade notices and local review paths.

applies_when: The template may affect enrolled repo behavior or future repo starts.
does_not_apply_when: The edit is local wording with no contract, cadence, or managed-surface effect.
rules.danger_if_missed: Downstream repos retain stale instructions and miss new capture obligations.

rules.description: A structured review workflow created reusable DAD mail or issue logic but exposed an exception-lake or governance gap.

emit.rationale: The LawFirm-os-intake missed-capture specimen should create both workflow mail and an exception seed automatically.

applies_when: A review workflow yields reusable structure plus a gap DAD should learn from.
does_not_apply_when: The review is private, unstructured, or has no reusable workflow/gap evidence.
rules.danger_if_missed: Lowell has to notice the pattern manually and DAD fails to learn from review work.

rules.description: A repo produced a reusable architecture reference, design pattern, or buildout map.

emit.rationale: Reusable architecture references should be offered to DAD for future repo consults.

applies_when: The design can help new repos or repo families.
does_not_apply_when: The design is source-specific and unsafe to summarize.
rules.danger_if_missed: Future repos miss proven architecture patterns.

rules.description: Governance map, source authority, managed path, or human gate drift is observed.

emit.rationale: Governance drift should be visible to DAD and target repos without mutating source authority.

applies_when: A governance or managed-surface contract differs from reviewed DAD policy.
does_not_apply_when: The difference is expected local source authority and no DAD contract is involved.
rules.danger_if_missed: DAD can apply stale governance assumptions to protected or public repos.

rules.description: A governed artifact was added or changed but not registered into the manifests, suites, generated snapshots, AI navigation, catalogs, or maps that make it discoverable and enforceable.

emit.rationale: Registration drift creates false-green governance: the new artifact can validate locally while future agents, suites, manifests, or catalogs never see it.

applies_when: An agent adds or changes a schema, validator, generated report, template, red-team fixture, governance config, asset catalog entry, workflow map, data map, prompt, review intake, or reusable workflow asset.
does_not_apply_when: The artifact is a scratch note, generated cache, temporary local experiment, or intentionally ungoverned file documented as excluded from future-agent routing.
rules.danger_if_missed: Future agents may miss the artifact, validators may pass stale evidence, DAD may not discover a reusable asset, and readiness claims may rely on incomplete manifests or suite output.

rules.description: A data movement or sensitivity-boundary issue affects DAD mail, public release, or exception capture.

emit.rationale: Data-boundary changes must be candidate notices and exception events because they can leak private context.

applies_when: DAD movement rules or public/private boundaries may be affected.
does_not_apply_when: The data is local-only and unrelated to DAD movement or public-facing repos.
rules.danger_if_missed: Private-origin context could reach public-facing repos without release.

rules.description: DAD mail itself needs a new message type, field, route, cadence, or dedupe behavior.

emit.rationale: Mail contract changes need DAD review and capture-surface update tests.

applies_when: An observed repo need requires new DAD mail fields or behavior.
does_not_apply_when: The existing mail schema handles the case safely.
rules.danger_if_missed: Repos keep sending incomplete packets after DAD's needs change.

rules.description: A command failed and the repo can emit safe command metadata without raw output.

emit.rationale: Failed commands are useful learning seeds when captured as argv, exit code, and safe refs instead of stdout/stderr.

applies_when: A command exits non-zero or is explicitly treated as failed by the repo workflow.
does_not_apply_when: The command output would be the only evidence or safe metadata cannot identify the failure class.
rules.danger_if_missed: Repeated command failures stay trapped in chat or terminal output and DAD cannot learn fixes.

rules.description: A test failed or timed out and the repo can emit suite/test metadata without raw assertions.

emit.rationale: DAD needs test-failure metadata to learn orchestration and harness gaps without collecting private fixtures or assertion bodies.

applies_when: A unit, integration, parity, or validation test fails and can be referenced safely by path or test id.
does_not_apply_when: The failure evidence requires private row data, raw snapshots, or long assertion bodies.
rules.danger_if_missed: Test failures repeat across repos and slow-test/parity harness opportunities are lost.

rules.description: A CLI, script, service, or app raised a runtime exception and safe top-frame metadata is available.

emit.rationale: Runtime exceptions are high-value learning seeds when represented by class, fingerprint, and safe code refs instead of full stack traces.

applies_when: An uncaught or material runtime exception interrupts work and can be summarized by class and path pointer.
does_not_apply_when: The stack trace or request payload contains sensitive data that cannot be reduced to safe refs.
rules.danger_if_missed: DAD cannot connect runtime failures to fixes, tests, or harness improvements.

rules.description: A required local CLI, tool, plugin, or skill was unavailable and a governed fallback was used.

emit.rationale: Missing tools such as asset-dir not on PATH should become exception metadata so DAD can improve enrollment and fallback guidance.

applies_when: A repo agent cannot run a required tool and must use a fallback path or alter the plan.
does_not_apply_when: The tool is optional and no workflow changed.
rules.danger_if_missed: Fallbacks stay invisible and DAD cannot repair install, PATH, or enrollment guidance.

rules.description: A repo rename or path move may affect DAD return addresses, usage ledgers, mail routing, or enrollment identity.

emit.rationale: Repo renames must preserve stable repo identity and mail return addresses so DAD does not fork history by path.

applies_when: A persistent repo is renamed, moved, or changes its DAD return address.
does_not_apply_when: A temporary clone, archive copy, or throwaway path changes without DAD enrollment or usage history.
rules.danger_if_missed: DAD can misdeliver mail, lose usage history, or duplicate a repo after a rename.

rules.description: A repo split, copy, or extraction creates multiple descendant repos that need separate DAD enrollment and lineage.

emit.rationale: Repo splits must not silently reuse one repo identity across multiple source authorities.

applies_when: A persistent repo is split, copied into a new persistent repo, or extracted into child repos.
does_not_apply_when: A disposable worktree, temp clone, or backup copy is explicitly outside DAD enrollment.
rules.danger_if_missed: Mail, usage history, and exception fixes can cross source-authority boundaries after a split.

rules.description: A write to a protected repo was blocked, or should have been blocked, because explicit local-write approval was missing.

emit.rationale: Protected repo write blocks must be first-class exception evidence so DAD cannot quietly normalize unsafe local writes.

applies_when: DAD, an agent, hook, enrollment update, or mail delivery attempted or considered a write outside the approved protected-repo boundary.
does_not_apply_when: The repo is not protected, the write is ordinary mailbox-only delivery allowed by policy, or a reviewed approval explicitly authorizes the write.
rules.danger_if_missed: DAD can accidentally mutate Logos or another protected repo without leaving a reviewable safety record.

rules.description: Enrollment, update, delivery, release, or repair work was blocked because the target repo had uncommitted work or an unsafe branch state.

emit.rationale: Dirty worktree blocks protect active source-authority work and should be visible without copying diffs.

applies_when: A DAD enrollment, update, public release, protected repair, mail delivery, or other governance operation stops because the repo is dirty or on an unsafe branch.
does_not_apply_when: The operation is read-only, the repo policy explicitly allows the dirty state, or the dirty state is unrelated to the blocked operation.
rules.danger_if_missed: Agents may overwrite active work or repeatedly retry blocked governance operations without understanding why.

rules.description: Private, internal, restricted, or unknown-origin data tried to move toward a public-facing target without explicit human release.

emit.rationale: Private-to-public movement attempts must be captured as blocked metadata so release gates can be audited without copying the private payload.

applies_when: Any mail, exception, lesson, asset, harness, template, enrollment notice, or source-packet candidate from a non-public origin targets a public-facing repo without human release.
does_not_apply_when: The target is not public-facing, the source is reviewed public-safe, or an explicit human release record authorizes the movement.
rules.danger_if_missed: Private-origin metadata or context could reach public-facing repos without a release audit trail.

rules.description: A generated report, structured test report, audit artifact, or methodology-dependent output failed freshness checks.

emit.rationale: Stale report failures are a false-confidence risk and should be captured with hash refs rather than report bodies.

applies_when: A validator, parity checker, report freshness gate, or audit finds that a report predates its inputs, run start time, methodology, or expected hash.
does_not_apply_when: The report is intentionally historical, clearly labeled stale candidate evidence, or has already been regenerated and validated.
rules.danger_if_missed: Agents can trust stale reports, old test output, or outdated methodology evidence and make false-green decisions.

rules.description: A JSONL row failed parsing and was quarantined or skipped with only safe location and hash metadata.

emit.rationale: Malformed mailbox, exception, or fix-outcome rows should be learnable without copying the raw broken line.

applies_when: A repo, DAD collector, digest, archive, or validator detects a malformed JSONL row and can record safe path, line, hash, and quarantine refs.
does_not_apply_when: The only useful evidence would require copying the malformed raw line, private row, credential, or long payload into DAD.
rules.danger_if_missed: Malformed rows can silently remove repo learning, mail, or exception events from DAD while validators appear healthy.

rules.description: A duplicate mail delivery was detected and acknowledged instead of being delivered as a new suggestion.

emit.rationale: Duplicate mail is usually benign, but repeated duplicates reveal routing, dedupe, or retry behavior DAD should calibrate.

applies_when: A DAD mail collect, route, deliver, digest, or repo-local mailbox process observes a repeated mail_id or dedupe_key and writes an ack/archive instead of a new inbox item.
does_not_apply_when: The delivery is a legitimate follow-up thread message, a new dedupe key, or the payload itself would need to be copied to prove duplication.
rules.danger_if_missed: DAD can spam repos or hide delivery-loop defects because duplicate handling never enters the exception lake.

rules.description: Pytest timing, collection, or orchestration evidence shows a slow-test hotspot or improvement candidate.

emit.rationale: Slow pytest evidence should feed the Python test orchestration and Rust-shadow harnesses without pretending speed claims are proven.

applies_when: A repo observes slow pytest runs, expensive full batteries, fixture bottlenecks, or candidate selection/sharding opportunities with safe timing refs.
does_not_apply_when: There is no timing evidence, no stable test scope, or the report would require raw private fixture data or long logs.
rules.danger_if_missed: Agents may keep running expensive suites blindly or propose Rust without profiling and same-scope validation evidence.

rules.description: A required validation command, dependency, tool, or environment capability was missing for the attempted change.

emit.rationale: Missing validation commands should become DAD learning so enrollment, templates, dependencies, and fallback guidance can improve.

applies_when: An agent cannot run a required validation command or expected checker because the command, dependency, tool, plugin, or environment capability is unavailable.
does_not_apply_when: The command is optional, not relevant to the changed surface, or a safe equivalent validation command was already run and recorded.
rules.danger_if_missed: Repos may appear validated when the key command never ran, and DAD cannot repair templates or dependency guidance.

rules.description: A DAD recommendation, context-pack item, mail suggestion, asset, skill, template, or harness advice was harmful, misleading, unsafe, or wasteful.

emit.rationale: Harmful DAD advice must feed the calibration ledger and exception lake so context packs and offerings can be corrected.

applies_when: A repo tried, followed, or seriously evaluated a DAD recommendation and found it harmful, unsafe, misleading, or wasteful.
does_not_apply_when: The recommendation was merely irrelevant, saved for future, or safely ignored without adverse effect.
rules.danger_if_missed: DAD keeps recommending harmful guidance because negative outcomes never enter calibration.

rules.description: A repo attempted to use a DAD asset, harness, skill, or template and the attempt failed or could not be validated.

emit.rationale: Failed asset attempts show where DAD guidance, harnesses, templates, or checkout instructions need repair.

applies_when: A DAD asset, harness, skill, or template was selected for current use and failed validation, install, checkout, or adoption.
does_not_apply_when: The repo only saved the asset for future, rejected it before trying it, or the failure was unrelated to the DAD surface.
rules.danger_if_missed: DAD assets look useful in catalogs but fail silently when repos actually try them.

rules.description: A required or high-priority DAD recommendation, stop condition, learning-rule acknowledgement, or non-negotiable was ignored or bypassed.

emit.rationale: Ignored hard guidance needs explicit evidence so DAD can distinguish justified local authority from agent drift.

applies_when: A required DAD rule, context-pack recommendation, stop condition, or acknowledgement was skipped, bypassed, or left unresolved.
does_not_apply_when: A candidate-only optional recommendation was locally rejected with ordinary adoption tracking.
rules.danger_if_missed: Agents can drift around hard gates and DAD cannot calibrate which rules are unrealistic or being ignored.

rules.description: A local screening gate detected credential-like, PII-like, or private-row content and only safe block metadata may leave the repo.

emit.rationale: DAD needs to know that a safety gate fired without receiving the sensitive payload that triggered it.

applies_when: A local screening gate blocks outbound exception, mail, lesson, harness, or report content because the payload appears sensitive.
does_not_apply_when: The packet contains the sensitive value itself, raw rows, logs, credentials, or source blobs; those signals must be suppressed or quarantined locally.
rules.danger_if_missed: Sensitive-data prevention events stay invisible and DAD cannot improve public/private gates or downstream guidance.

rules.description: A local screening gate rejected raw logs, stack traces, tables, diffs, source blobs, transcripts, or other oversized content.

emit.rationale: Raw blob rejection is a useful capture-quality signal when represented by class, hash/ref, and replacement summary only.

applies_when: A local packet or review tried to include raw logs, stack traces, table-like rows, diffs, source blobs, or transcripts and the gate replaced them with metadata.
does_not_apply_when: The raw content is still present in the outbound packet or the payload is a short safe metadata field.
rules.danger_if_missed: Agents may repeatedly try to move raw evidence into DAD, creating privacy and noise risks without a learning signal.

rules.description: A data-only payload included prompt-injection-like text and was kept inert as safe block metadata.

emit.rationale: Prompt-injection-like source content should be tracked as inert evidence without ever becoming executable agent instruction.

applies_when: A repo-local gate detects instruction-like text inside data, review payloads, mail, exception packets, or source material.
does_not_apply_when: The outbound record would quote the instruction-like text itself or ask another agent to follow it.
rules.danger_if_missed: Untrusted source text may be copied into DAD surfaces without an explicit inert-data boundary.

rules.description: A downstream artifact kept an upstream id but dropped semantic fields needed by later workflow, safety, scoring, review, or control-plane layers.

emit.rationale: Lineage field drops should be captured as safe metadata so DAD can improve validators and downstream architecture guidance without collecting private source rows.

applies_when: A derived artifact has a valid upstream id but omits fields required for later behavior, validation, or safety decisions.
does_not_apply_when: The downstream artifact is intentionally id-only and a validator proves every consumer dereferences the upstream record before use.
rules.danger_if_missed: A repo can look lineage-aware while silently losing semantic data that future layers depend on.

rules.description: A first demo, matter, case, client, dataset, or prototype contaminated reusable architecture or future intake defaults.

emit.rationale: Prototype-to-product contamination should notify DAD and record an exception because it can make future repos or cases inherit hidden source assumptions.

applies_when: Case-specific paths, names, defaults, prompts, configs, docs, or outputs leak into reusable root architecture or next-case workflow.
does_not_apply_when: The artifact is intentionally case-scoped under a case_id output root and cannot affect reusable architecture.
rules.danger_if_missed: The first successful output becomes the hidden parent architecture for future work.

rules.description: Judgment-heavy external review or Fable/Claude/human feedback stayed in chat or mutated work without a governed advisory intake and acceptance gate.

emit.rationale: Hard-problem review should enter DAD as advisory candidate evidence with an explicit acceptance gate instead of becoming hidden chat memory.

applies_when: A repo gets judgment-heavy external AI or human review for realism, ethics, strategy, readiness, or safety and no governed review intake captures the recommendation boundary.
does_not_apply_when: The review already has an advisory intake, source-authority boundary, and deterministic acceptance or rejection record.
rules.danger_if_missed: High-leverage review advice is lost in chat or over-applied as source truth without local acceptance evidence.

rules.description: A new exception type or capture contract is needed.

emit.rationale: Unknown exception patterns should create a taxonomy suggestion and a candidate exception event.

applies_when: Existing exception taxonomy cannot represent the observed safe metadata.
does_not_apply_when: A reviewed event type already fits.
rules.danger_if_missed: Novel failure classes collapse into `other` and cannot be learned from.

rules.description: A red-team, premortem, Fable, Claude, Codex, Cursor, security, or human review found a material issue.

emit.rationale: Material review findings are exception-lake seeds even before a code failure occurs.

applies_when: The finding affects correctness, governance, safety, privacy, or future-agent behavior.
does_not_apply_when: The review is only style preference or duplicates an existing event.
rules.danger_if_missed: DAD cannot learn from external review feedback.

rules.description: An exception was fixed, accepted, rejected, reopened, or rolled back with evidence.

emit.rationale: The lake learns from fixes only when outcomes and validation refs are recorded.

applies_when: A tracked event has a closure, fix, validation, accepted-risk, or rollback decision.
does_not_apply_when: No event is tracked or the closure lacks validation/rationale.
rules.danger_if_missed: DAD accumulates open failures without learning which fixes worked.

rules.description: A task produced a reusable lesson, DAD need, offering update, or context-pack calibration signal.

emit.rationale: Reusable learning should be routed as bounded candidate mail and, when missed by the agent, as an exception event.

applies_when: The lesson affects future agent task order, DAD offerings, or capture rules.
does_not_apply_when: The observation is routine, duplicate, hidden reasoning, or not reusable.
rules.danger_if_missed: DAD repeats the same mistake because the lesson never enters the loop.

authority_boundary: Capture rules are deterministic tests for expected repo emissions. They do not prove truth, approve public release, or authorize DAD to mutate target repositories.
